![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/cd279c5acb398853188a3b2cc50fd3897d5a4ef84edc8d628b810ac0063e3b11.png)

The Venn diagram shown above represents two events $G$ and $F$ and the probabilities of each event. $G$ represents the event that a student of certain college studies German, and $F$ represents the event that a student of this college studies French. Find the probability that a randomly selected student who studies French also studies German.
question.worked_solution:
We wish to compute the probability that a student studies German *given that* they study French. Therefore, we need to compute $P(G|F).$ 

To compute $P(G|F),$ we need to ask, "what is the probability of $G$ occurring given that $F$ has occurred?"

Since we are assuming that $F$ has occurred, we only consider the events inside $F.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/e212b753cbcf6b5ffe20c418ebc01516eee6ae7460eba948989d5e37273036b7.png)

The probability of event $F$ occurring is

$$
P(F)=0.3+0.2=0.5.
$$

Now, $P(G|F)$ can be interpreted as the proportion of $G$ that lies inside $F,$ relative to the size of $F.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G|F) & =\frac{0.3}{0.5}=0.6.\end{aligned}
$$
